title: Cuban-Spiced Pork Medallions with Black Beans and Rice
intro: Pairing lean pork with a base of black beans and brown rice delivers helpful fiber and steady-digesting carbohydrates to keep your energy stable. Slicing the tenderloin into thin medallions ensures it cooks rapidly without drying out.

ingredients.name: Pork tenderloin
ingredients.canonical_name: Pork, fresh, loin, tenderloin, separable lean only, raw

ingredients.name: No-salt-added canned black beans
ingredients.canonical_name: Beans, black, mature seeds, canned, low sodium

instructions: Toss the pork medallions with the cumin, oregano, and black pepper in a bowl to coat evenly.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork in a single layer and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, flipping halfway, until the meat is browned, then transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the red onion and green bell pepper to the skillet. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables soften.
Stir the minced garlic into the skillet and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the rinsed black beans, brown rice, and water to the pan. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the mixture is steaming and heated through.
Remove the skillet from the heat. Stir in the fresh lime juice, then return the pork medallions and resting juices to the pan, tossing gently to combine.
Divide the rice and vegetable mixture evenly between warm plates, and top with the pork medallions.
variation: Swap the pork tenderloin for boneless, skinless chicken breast pieces.
conservation: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat in the microwave until warmed through.
